text: After summarizing Khan et al.'s finding that persuasiveness-trained LLM debaters help non-expert judges, the authors note that this line of work mainly uses QuALITY, where justifications are mostly verified quotes. They contrast it with their own focus on a less artificial reasoning domain where the prover-verifier difference is a capability gap rather than privileged information.
title: Kirchner et al. call Khan et al.'s QuALITY debate setting artificial: privileged information, not capability gap
